message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Build, Lint & Test

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches:
    - master

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version-file: .nvmrc
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Lint
        run: pnpm run lint
      - name: Validate test fixtures
        uses: nhalstead/validate-json-action@v0.1.12
        with:
          schema: tests/fixtures/schema.json
          jsons: tests/fixtures/*/*.json
      - name: Test
        run: pnpm test
      - name: Build
        run: pnpm run build",
  "rationale": "Add a custom job timeout (timeout-minutes: 5) to bound runaway job consumption while preserving every existing build, lint, fixture-validation, and test step. The repository's CI history shows successful runs completing in roughly 31-106 seconds, so a 5-minute limit provides operational headroom without risking false timeouts on valid slow runs. The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern is supported by a measured fork experiment (26.82% elapsed savings, all 3 runs successful) and by literature reporting estimated VM time reduction (12.9% free, 8.1% paid). Preconditions are met: representative successful-duration history exists, and no contraindication applies because valid runs are far below the proposed limit.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508", "pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT"]
}

```

This already caches pnpm dependencies. So adding another cache might be redundant.

2. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (Bound jobs with a custom timeout) - evidence_type: simulation_estimate, reported_result: vm_time_reduction_percent free 12.9, paid 8.1. Preconditions: Representative successful-duration history exists. The CI history shows runs with durations around 30-31 seconds (created_at to updated_at). The experiment example for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT shows baseline median_elapsed_seconds 41.0, optimized 30.0, with timeout-minutes: 5.

- run 38551007214: 10:38:39 to 10:39:14 = 35 seconds
- run 38465231160: 20:44:44 to 20:46:02 = 78 seconds
- run 38464791919: 20:41:11 to 20:42:57 = 106 seconds

So runs are relatively fast (31-106 seconds). A custom timeout of 5 minutes would be reasonable headroom.

The experiment example for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (document_id: experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508) shows:
- Before: no timeout-minutes
- After: timeout-minutes: 5 added to the job
- Metrics: baseline median_elapsed 41.0s, optimized 30.0s, 26.8% savings

This is a measured experiment on a fork. The pattern P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT has preconditions: "Representative successful-duration history exists". The CI history shows successful runs with durations, so this precondition is met.

The contraindications: "Valid slow runs exceed the proposed limit". With runs taking 31-106 seconds, a 5-minute timeout is plenty of headroom.

This seems like a good fit. The optimization is to add `timeout-minutes: 5` to the job. This bounds runaway consumption without changing build/test coverage.

- experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508 (measured CI workflow on fork, P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT)
- pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (literature report)

name: Build, Lint & Test

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches:
    - master

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version-file: .nvmrc
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Lint
        run: pnpm run lint
      - name: Validate test fixtures
        uses: nhalstead/validate-json-action@v0.1.12
        with:
          schema: tests/fixtures/schema.json
          jsons: tests/fixtures/*/*.json
      - name: Test
        run: pnpm test
      - name: Build
        run: pnpm run build
```

This is a minimal change that adds a custom timeout. Evidence supports it (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT with measured 26.8% elapsed savings in the experiment, and literature reporting 12.9% free / 8.1% paid VM time reduction).

The rationale: The CI history shows successful runs completing well under 5 minutes (31-106 seconds), so a 5-minute timeout provides headroom without risking false timeouts on valid slow runs. The experiment evidence shows this pattern reduced elapsed time by ~26.8% on a measured fork, and the literature pattern reports estimated VM time reduction. All build/lint/test steps are preserved.

Evidence IDs: 
- experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508
- pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT

Let me make sure I'm not weakening permissions or adding privileged actions. Adding timeout-minutes doesn't do any of that. It's a safety bound.

I'm confident in APPLY.
